svg.text: Figure 26. From hotter fuel to the Doppler requirement
Logic is Closed. The coefficient is Open. Do not invent pcm per degree or a k-effective.
1. More fissions
kernel heats first
2. Nuclei jiggle
Doppler broadening
3. Wider U-238 traps
more capture, less split
4. k falls
as T_fuel rises
5. Graphite can go the other way a little
Moderator-temperature coefficient can be slightly positive
in some lattices. That is why Doppler alone is not the spec.
6. The requirement (Open: SCALE / MCNP)
Net power coefficient negative from 20 C to 750 C.
Hotter still means less splitting overall.
7. Leftover splitting-power is a separate rule (DB-11)
Delayed neutrons are about 65 in 10,000 (thermal U-235 class). A dollar of reactivity is that share.
After shutdown margin, leftover excess stays under 0.8 dollars so one failure cannot go prompt-critical.
Shutdown margin at least 1.0 dollar with the most reactive drum stuck withdrawn. No made-up k-effective in this book.
House sentence
If the core tries to run away, heat itself applies the brake in milliseconds, without a person or a motor. That brake lives in the uranium, not in an app.
What would count as shown
A lattice run with packing fraction, C/U, enrichment, poisons, and drums: negative net power coefficient, plus the Chapter 8 section 3.4 k-effective table.
This drawing is the chain. It is not the coefficient.
